convention.what: Parts of the product that are on screen but not finished, which this manual therefore documents around without naming.
convention.why: Describing such a control as working lies to the reader; describing it as broken publishes a product defect inside a client-facing document. Neither is the author's call, so the manual waits.
convention.whoActs: Whoever finishes the product. An entry is closed by deleting its `pending` declaration from the section that declares it, once the content it withheld has been written.
convention.declaredIn: the `pending` list of a section under manuals/<manual>/sections/ — never in the rendered manual, which names none of this
convention.notDone: a section with an entry here is NOT complete by the module-completeness standard, and must not be counted as done

All of it renders: the panel uses `createFullColumns` (:150).

Its two tabs, the ten columns of the programming table and its filters, the nine columns of the resources table and its search, the procedure that dispatches a resource to a case, and the two dispatch states. The code here is fully wired with no fixture path anywhere: it calls four real endpoints — `prt-api.adapter.ts:46` (`/api/prt/programacion`) and `resources-api.adapter.ts:15`, :29 and :50 (`/prt/resource-managment`, `/prt/resource-pj-flag`, `/prt/resource-dispatch`).
